feasibility_verdict: CONDITIONAL GO — mechanism yes, current head no. The integration is small, cleanly gateable, and the dawdle probe shows the calibrated utility is SAFE (0% conversion-control flips up to k=1.0, 0% midgame flips to k=0.5, median v-cost of a flip <0.001). But it must NOT ship against the m4c12 head (chance-level within-game ordering, wrong-sign sibling decrements — it would steer search BACKWARD), and even a healed head only carries a coarse conversion-zone (<60 true moves-left) gradient. So: build the plumbing defaults-off now, enable only behind a head-heal + re-audit stamp, and scope expectations to 'wins convert faster inside the conversion zone' — this utility will NOT see marathons coming ([120+) bias -111..-194) and is not the fix for marathon onset; it is a fix for dawdling at already-decided positions, which is where the measured squandering lives.
utility_design:
FORMULA (Lc0-style moves-left utility; 'KataGo-style' per owner framing — |v|-scaled, saturating, delta-based). Applied as a SELECTION-TIME bonus inside PUCT edge scoring at packages/hexo_models/dense_cnn/rust/src/mcts_tree.rs:609 (select_or_materialize_edge), NOT as Q-target shaping at backprop. Per materialized edge e of node n:

  score(e) = Q_fpu(e) + U_ml(e) + c_puct * P(e) * sqrt(N_n) / (1 + N_e)
  U_ml(e)  = - w_ml * g(Q_e) * tanh( (M_e - M_n) / m_scale )
  g(q)     = sign(q) * clamp((|q| - q_thresh) / (1 - q_thresh), 0, 1), with the losing side multiplied by lose_side_scale (default 0.0 = win-side-only)

where M_e = edge moves-left stat (ml_sum_e / ml_weight_e, real backups only; U_ml = 0 when ml_weight_e == 0, FPU-neutral), M_n = same stat at the node (the sibling baseline), Q_e = edge.value_or_fpu from the node player's perspective. Defaults: w_ml = 0.03 (value units, hard cap on |U_ml| via tanh), q_thresh = 0.6, m_scale = 32 decisions (4 head bins), lose_side_scale = 0.0.

CALIBRATION FROM THE PROBE: the probe's safe band was k in [0.2, 0.5] on U = v - k*sign(v)*ml/512, i.e. per-decision slope 3.9e-4..9.8e-4. This formula's small-delta slope is w_ml*g/m_scale: at |Q|=0.8 (g=0.5) that is 4.7e-4 (~probe k=0.24); at |Q|->1 it is 9.4e-4 (~k=0.48) — inside the validated envelope at both ends. The tanh cap bounds total bonus at 0.03, below the healthy-control median best-to-2nd v-gap of 0.065, so healthy conversion choices cannot flip even in the worst case — matching the measured 0% collateral.

WHY DELTA-vs-NODE-BASELINE: the head's only validated signal is the relative sibling gradient (spread std ~5, range 18-20, correct sign on healthy ckpts); its absolute output is bias-ridden (mean-decode +28..+58 near the end, +25 cross-move jump, marathon output a constant ~90-110). The (M_e - M_n) form is invariant to per-position absolute bias by construction. Median-of-bins decode (not mean) on the Python side removes the right-skew overestimate near game end.

WHY SELECTION-TIME, NOT BACKPROP Q-SHAPING: (1) value purity — value_sum at mcts_tree.rs:718 feeds FPU parent values, recorded root q diagnostics, and prune_forced_delta_counts; shaping it would leak ml signal into value-adjacent training/diagnostic surfaces and into the eval cache semantics (RustEvaluation.value is cached/shared via Arc). (2) Virtual loss — apply_virtual_visit (mcts_tree.rs:691) subtracts virtual_loss from value_sum on visit; keeping ml in separate (ml_sum, ml_weight) fields updated ONLY at real backup means in-flight virtual visits never dilute M, with zero new virtual-loss interaction. (3) Coverage — terminal, TSS-proven, and existing-node backups (mcts.rs:1301-1321) bypass NN eval; node-stat ml with a depth offset handles terminals EXACTLY (ml = 0 + path distance), and terminal-proximity is precisely the conversion zone where the head is strongest and the pressure is wanted. (4) PCR fast searches (greedy, pcr_fast_visits, no noise) are steered identically through the same scoring loop with bounded magnitude. Final move selection is visits-based (visit_policy, mcts.rs:2132-2159), so shifting visits is sufficient and no root-selection change is needed.

ML BACKUP SEMANTICS: backup_virtual gains leaf_ml: Option<f32>; at path step i the contribution is leaf_ml + (path_len - i) — a per-step depth offset in DECISIONS, perspective-free (never negated). Leaf sources: terminal -> 0.0 exact; existing_node -> node.ml(); TSS-proven verdict -> None (skip ml backup, phase 1); NN leaf -> RustEvaluation.moves_left (median-decoded scalar from Python). Unvisited staged candidates (the materialization branch at mcts_tree.rs:627) keep their pure prior*exploration score — no ml term.

PIVOT / PREREQUISITE (probes say the current head is NOT usable): (a) heal the head — cheapest path is simply later main_4 checkpoints trained on post-quarantine data (loss already recovering 3.65->3.36 by ep13); re-run the existing audit scripts (scripts/_wf_s3_mlaudit.py + _wf_s3d_probe.py, CPU, hours) against ep14+ until the gate passes: conv(<60) within-game rho >= 0.6, [0,5) median-decode MAE <= 15, end-vs-mid pairwise >= 0.85, correct-sign sibling decrements at ml=10/30/60. (b) Training-side head fixes if healing stalls (no Rust): resolve the plies-vs-decisions target-unit ambiguity in npz moves_left (main_3 shards look plies-like: ml + turn_index == game length, max 853; samples.py defines decisions) — MANDATORY before search use since the Rust depth offset counts decisions; raise moves_left_weight 0.1 -> 0.3-0.5 in losses.py:142 to fight range compression (predictions span [8,190] of [0,512]); optionally log-spaced bin edges for conversion-zone resolution (bigger change, re-inits the head — defer). The head stays a Linear(64->65) on the shared aux ValueReduction; no architecture change is required for this design.

integration_layers.changes: Add RestnetNetwork.forward_policy_value_moves_left: trunk once, then policy_head + value_head(value_reduction) + aux_value_reduction -> moves_left_head ONLY (skips opp_policy and stvalue_* heads; extra compute is one conv1x1+Linear(1681->64)+Linear(64->65), negligible). Leave forward_policy_value (architecture.py:857-864) byte-for-byte untouched — it is the default inference ABI and the TRT/torch.compile/fp16-gate target. Add decode_binned_moves_left(logits) in losses.py next to decode_binned_value (losses.py:26): MEDIAN-of-bins decode (first bin where CDF >= 0.5) mapped onto [0, MOVES_LEFT_CAP=512] and clamped — per the audit, median decode is materially better than mean near game end. DenseCNNInference gains export_moves_left: bool = False; when True, evaluate_model1_payload (inference.py:337-412) calls the new forward, includes the moves_left head in the chunked-batch concat (inference.py:356-361), and returns one extra key 'moves_left_bytes' (f32 row-major, one scalar per row, units = predicted remaining decisions, validated finite in [0, 512]). values_bytes/priors_bytes layout unchanged.
integration_layers.default_behavior: export_moves_left=False -> payload dict is byte-identical to today (no extra key, same forward path); guarded by a golden-digest test.

integration_layers.changes: RustEvaluation (mcts_eval.rs:103-110) gains moves_left: Option<f32>. The parse site (mcts_eval.rs:339-390) takes an ml_required flag threaded from the session config: when the utility is enabled, REQUIRE 'moves_left_bytes' with require_exact_bytes(rows, 4) and a read_moves_left mirroring read_value (mcts_eval.rs:609) that rejects non-finite or out-of-[0,1024] values (fail-loud, matching the existing values_bytes contract); when disabled, never touch the key, so old evaluators (and the no-moves-left wire format) remain the default and fully back-compatible. The shared eval cache carries the extra Option<f32> per Arc<RustEvaluation> (~8 bytes/entry, negligible).
integration_layers.default_behavior: Disabled -> parser identical to today; an evaluator that emits the extra key is silently ignored; an enabled session with an evaluator that omits the key aborts with a clear PyValueError.

integration_layers.layer: L3 — Tree stats, backup, selection bonus (mcts_tree.rs + mcts.rs)
integration_layers.changes: RustNode (mcts_tree.rs:126) += eval_ml: Option<f32>, ml_sum: f32, ml_weight: u32; RustEdge (mcts_tree.rs:47) += ml_sum: f32, ml_weight: u32 (+16 bytes/edge — visible in the existing active_edge_bytes diagnostic, fine at current scale). backup_virtual (mcts_tree.rs:703) gains leaf_ml: Option<f32>: per path step add leaf_ml + depth_offset (decisions, perspective-free, no negation) to node+edge ml_sum and increment ml_weight; apply_virtual_visit untouched (virtual visits never touch ml stats -> no in-flight dilution, no virtual-loss interaction). Leaf-ml sources at the four backup call sites (mcts.rs:1301-1331 batch path, 1391-1411 continuous path, 1352-1369/1465-1494 eval-attach paths): terminal -> Some(0.0); existing_node -> node.ml(); TSS verdict -> None; NN eval -> evaluation.moves_left. select_or_materialize_edge (mcts_tree.rs:577-657): add U_ml to the visited-edge score loop (line 609) per the formula; staged-candidate materialization and forced_root_edge unchanged. MovesLeftUtilityConfig {weight, q_threshold, scale, lose_side_scale, apply_in_fast} threaded into RustSearch alongside fpu_reduction. prune_forced_delta_counts (mcts.rs:2226) keeps its U_ml-free PUCT comparison in phase 1 (forced playouts exist only at noisy roots; bonus bounded at 0.03) — documented approximation, optional phase-2 consistency pass.

integration_layers.changes: TOML [selfplay.moves_left_utility]: enabled=false (master switch; also flips export_moves_left on the evaluator construction), weight=0.03, q_threshold=0.6, scale=32.0, lose_side_scale=0.0, apply_in_fast=true (PCR fast searches), apply_in_eval=true (eval/gating arena — symmetric by default, separable only for diagnosis). Parse in config.py next to the PCR knobs (config.py:224-234, parse at :442) with the existing unknown-key rejection. Plumb through selfplay.py (the run_continuous call sites at :649/:1508 and the diagnostics dicts at :1029/:1595), mcts.py:135, rust_bridge.py:102-175, and the PyO3 signature (mcts.rs:684) as Option-typed trailing args so older callers are unaffected. Validation mirrors pcr: weight in [0, 0.2], q_threshold in [0, 1), scale > 0. Phase 2 (separate task, only if the A/B wins and the perf hit matters): rebuild the TRT engine / compile graph with the third output.

integration_layers.layer: L0 — PREREQUISITE: head heal + re-audit (blocks enablement, not the build)
integration_layers.changes: (1) Resolve the plies-vs-decisions unit ambiguity in npz moves_left targets (main_3 shards: ml + turn_index == game length exactly, max 853 — plies-like; samples.py defines decisions-remaining) — the Rust depth offset assumes decisions, a 2x unit mismatch mis-scales every delta. (2) Heal: prefer simply auditing later main_4 checkpoints (ml loss recovering 3.65->3.36 by ep13) with the existing CPU audit scripts; if stalled after ~3 more epochs, raise moves_left_weight 0.1 -> 0.3-0.5 (losses.py:142) at the next training-config touchpoint. (3) Gate: conv(<60) within-game Spearman >= 0.6, [0,5) median-decode MAE <= 15, end-vs-mid pairwise >= 0.85, correct-sign sibling decrements at true_ml=10/30/60. No enablement without this stamp.
integration_layers.default_behavior: Pure offline/training-side work; no search code depends on it landing — the utility simply stays off until the gate passes.
integration_layers.effort: 0.5 day script reuse per audit; weight change is a one-line config edit; elapsed time dominated by main_4's own training schedule (days)

validation_ladder: 1. Rust unit tests (cargo test, packages/hexo_models/dense_cnn/rust): ml backup depth-offset arithmetic incl. terminal leaf -> exact (0 + distance); perspective-free accumulation (no negation); ml_weight increments only on real backups — apply_virtual_visit leaves M unchanged; U_ml table-driven (winning prefers smaller M, lose_side_scale=0 zeroes the losing side, |q|<=q_thresh dead-zone, tanh saturation at +-weight, ml_weight==0 -> 0); wire parse: enabled+missing moves_left_bytes -> PyValueError, disabled -> key ignored, exact byte-length and finiteness rejection; selection determinism (tie ordering by visits/action_id preserved).

2. Python unit tests (WSL venv — authoritative per repo convention): decode_binned_moves_left median decode vs brute-force CDF on synthetic distributions; payload contains moves_left_bytes iff export_moves_left; chunked-batch concat includes the ml head; GOLDEN-DIGEST: values_bytes/priors_bytes byte-identical with the flag off vs current build; fp16 adoption gate ml-parity bound.

3. Off-switch equivalence smoke (CPU, debug-worker pattern): one short selfplay run with enabled=false on the new binary vs the current binary — .hxr action sequences and npz digests must be identical. This is the mandatory pre-deploy gate because rebuilding the extension touches the binary the live-run machinery uses; never rebuild/swap while main_4 is live.

4. Head re-audit gate on the candidate checkpoint (re-run scripts/_wf_s3_mlaudit.py + the sibling probe, CPU, read-only): conv(<60) within-game rho >= 0.6, [0,5) median-decode MAE <= 15, end-vs-mid pairwise >= 0.85, correct-sign parent->child decrements at ml=10/30/60. The utility may not be enabled in any config without this stamp.

5. CPU position-probe acceptance — the dawdle probe rerun THROUGH the real Rust search (extend scripts/_wf_s3d_probe.py to drive Model1MctsSession at pcr_fast-like visit counts on the same 64 squander + 15 conversion + 24 midgame positions): PASS = 0/15 conversion-control move changes and 0/24 midgame changes at weight 0.03 and 0.06; >= 10% of squander-point move choices change toward lower searched-M at weight 0.03 with the healed head; report per-(ply, true-ml) bucket with n, game-clustered SEs.

6. 1-epoch GPU A/B (branched run dir, identical seeds/config except moves_left_utility.enabled; only after the live main_4 run is finished — never against the live process): metrics = dec/game median + p90 by game phase (not aggregate mean only), conversion hold rate (frozen-win-override trigger rate + lead-squander rate via the corpus miner), eval strength vs a fixed anchor (400-game match; no-regression bound: utility arm >= 48%), moves_left and value train-loss stability, value calibration drift (mean(v_pred) - mean(z)).

7. Staged enable: weight 0.03, selfplay+eval symmetric, 2-3 epochs watching dec/game trend and gating; then optionally 0.05. Predefined aborts: eval winrate drop > 3 points vs anchor, ANY conversion-control flip in the nightly position probe, dec/game p90 worsening two consecutive epochs.
risks: Head quality is the binding constraint (probe 1): m4c12 is flood-damaged and actively harmful (conv-zone rho 0.17, WRONG-SIGN sibling decrements -3.7/-19.1 — it would lengthen, not shorten); healthy heads have no per-ply resolution (adjacent monotonic rate 0.51-0.61), emit a constant in [60,120), and are blind at [120+) (bias -111..-194). The utility therefore CANNOT prevent marathons — it can only speed conversion inside the <60-decision zone. If the owner expects marathon prevention, this is the wrong lever and expectations must be reset.

Sign rudder unreliability (probe 2): the |v|>0.6 leader read predicted the actual winner only 48% of the time at squander points (to-move parity optimism: 26/26 turn-passing successors flip to ~ -v_base). A wrongly-aimed utility shortens losing games and lengthens winning ones. Mitigations baked in: q_thresh=0.6 on SEARCH-AVERAGED Q (materially better than the raw one-ply v the probe used), lose_side_scale=0 default (win-side-only pressure), tanh cap at 0.03 (below the 0.065 healthy control v-gap).

Cross-move ml discontinuity / parity contamination: controls showed a +25 median ml jump across turn-passing actions; the delta-vs-node-baseline form is only valid if a node's children share stm parity. Uniform in all 79 probed positions but not proven globally — add cheap telemetry counting parity-mixed sibling sets and suppress the bonus at any mixed node if the count is nonzero.

Training-target contamination by design: value_sum stays pure (selection-time bonus), but POLICY targets are visit-derived (visit_policy / pruned_visit_policy, mcts.rs:2132/2179), so utility-shifted visits intentionally enter the policy training target. Monitor policy CE; also prune_forced_delta_counts compares PUCT values WITHOUT U_ml in phase 1 — a small documented inconsistency at noisy roots only.

Eval-vs-selfplay asymmetry: enabling in selfplay but not the eval/gating arena trains on utility-shaped targets while gating a different policy; default is symmetric (apply_in_eval=true), with the asymmetric flag reserved for diagnosis runs only.

Interaction with C1 (frozen-win override) and C3 (length-decay row weighting): all three push toward shorter games; stacked enablement confounds attribution and risks over-correction (premature conversion attempts, value-target distortion). The A/B must hold C1/C3 fixed; if the utility works, consider RELAXING length-decay rather than stacking.

Live-run safety: any change here rebuilds the Rust extension and Python package used by the live main_4 GPU run — never rebuild or hot-swap while it runs; all defaults off; off-switch byte-equivalence (ladder step 3) is the mandatory deploy gate.

Moves-left unit ambiguity (plies vs decisions): main_3 npz targets are plies-like (ml + turn_index == game length, max 853 > cap) while samples.py defines decisions-remaining; the Rust depth-offset backup counts decisions. A ~2x unit mismatch mis-scales deltas and m_scale. Must be resolved (and the head retrained on consistent units) BEFORE enablement.

Performance/infra: TRT and torch.compile graphs are built on the 2-output forward_policy_value — phase 1 refuses adoption when export is on (GPU perf hit during the A/B, acceptable; evaluator is 84% of wall so quantify before staged enable); fp16 parity gate must cover the ml head; +16 bytes/edge tree memory is negligible at current diagnostics scale.

One-ply-probe-to-search gap: all calibration comes from a one-ply lookahead proxy; in full search the bonus compounds over subtree aggregation and could over- or under-steer relative to the probe's k-envelope — this is exactly what ladder step 5 (probe through the real search) and the 1-epoch A/B exist to catch before any multi-epoch enable.
effort: Code work ~5-7 engineer-days total: L1 Python export 0.5-1d; L2 Rust wire parse 0.5d; L3 tree stats + backup + selection bonus + PyO3 plumbing 1.5-2d; L4 config knobs 0.5-1d; L5 fp16/TRT coexistence phase-1 0.5d (TRT engine rebuild deferred, +1-2d later); validation ladder steps 1-5 (units, golden digests, off-switch smoke, probe-through-search harness) 1.5-2d, heavily reusing scripts/_wf_s3_mlaudit.py and _wf_s3d_probe.py. Prerequisite L0 (head heal + re-audit) is ~0.5d of script reuse per audit pass but elapsed-time dominated by main_4's own training schedule (days); the unit-ambiguity fix is ~0.5d and only takes effect on newly generated shards. GPU A/B: 0.5d setup + 1-2d runtime + 0.5d analysis, schedulable only after the live run completes. Realistic elapsed end-to-end: 2-3 weeks, gated almost entirely on head healing, not on engineering.
